legend.title: Trend minus the world land average (0.00) · mm/day per decade

caption: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) EVLAND · 1981–2025 · Sen's slope of yearly means in each 2° square, after subtracting the world land average of the same year (its own trend: 0.00 mm/day per decade). Differences are in mm/day, not in percent of the local average. Strong colour: passes the map-wide test for false alarms (Mann-Kendall with memory correction, q = 0.05). This map enlarges areas near the poles.

processing: read the whole globe for the variable from the temporal (location-chunked) store, in latitude bands covering the full time axis
coarsened to 2 deg cells with edges at multiples of 2 from -90 / -180
yearly means of complete years 1981–2025 in each 2° square
minus the world land average of the same year (area-weighted mean of every square with a complete record)
per-square Sen's slope and Mann-Kendall (Yue-Wang), BH FDR across squares (trend_stats.py)
provenance.caveat: Data: MERRA-2 reanalysis, a weather model corrected by observations, about 50 km squares (the map averages them into 2° squares). The trend is a straight line through 1981–2025; it shows what changed, not why.
